description: A responsive in-browser planar two-body orbit planner. Users select Earth, Moon, or Mars, choose altitude and a tangential-speed factor, apply quick-start presets, animate a spacecraft, and inspect period, periapsis, apoapsis, eccentricity, and a live state readout. The display distinguishes bound ellipses from escape trajectories.

tests.result: PASS: 4 tests, 4 passed, 0 failed. Checks circular orbit inverse elements/period/energy; eccentric state round-trip and period closure; specific-energy and angular-momentum invariance across 101 propagated samples; and rejection of open orbits by the ellipse propagator. Tolerances are encoded in the rerunnable test file (including position 1e-7 km and velocity 1e-9 km/s after one period).

physicsAssumptions: Two-dimensional inertial frame with a point-mass central body and constant standard gravitational parameter; units are km, s, and km/s.
State-to-elements conversion uses specific mechanical energy, specific angular momentum, and the eccentricity vector.
Closed-orbit propagation solves elliptic Kepler's equation iteratively; ellipse propagation requires a > 0 and 0 <= e < 1.
Animation advances simulated time at 60 seconds per wall-clock second.
No atmosphere, thrust, perturbations, inclination, body rotation, finite body shape, or live ephemerides. Escape paths are flagged and not integrated/drawn as conic trajectories.
